due.label: Continuous pressure in CPAP/PEEP
due.summary: CPAP/PEEP delivers a set continuous pressure that remains the same during inspiration and exhalation; you dial in a pressure rather than a volume or rate.
due.userTake: You dial in a pressure, not a volume — it stays the same whether the patient is breathing in or breathing out.

due.projectTitle: Mechanical Ventilation Explained Clearly by MedCram.com | 2 of 5
due.label: PEEP alveolar recruitment
due.summary: PEEP keeps small distal airways and alveolar clusters open and recruited at end-exhalation, preventing collapse to zero pressure.
due.userTake: PEEP holds the little alveolar clusters open at the end of exhale instead of letting them collapse — turning up PEEP recruits more of them.

due.projectTitle: Mechanical Ventilation Explained Clearly by MedCram.com | 2 of 5
due.label: CPAP vs PEEP terminology
due.summary: CPAP is the term used when continuous positive pressure is delivered non-invasively via a mask; PEEP is the term for the same concept delivered through an invasive ventilator with an endotracheal tube.
due.userTake: CPAP is the non-invasive name (mask) and PEEP is the invasive name (through a ventilator/ET tube) for the same continuous-pressure idea.

due.projectTitle: Mechanical Ventilation Explained Clearly by MedCram.com | 2 of 5
due.label: CPAP = non-invasive, PEEP = invasive
due.insight: CPAP refers to continuous positive airway pressure delivered non-invasively via a face mask, while PEEP refers to the same continuous-pressure concept applied through an invasive ventilator circuit with an endotracheal tube.

transformed.front:
A patient requires positive pressure via a face mask without an endotracheal tube. Which therapy is this?
A) PEEP
B) CPAP
C) Ventilator
D) Invasive PEEP
transformed.why: CPAP is delivered non-invasively via a face mask, whereas PEEP uses an invasive ventilator circuit with an endotracheal tube.

due.projectTitle: Mechanical Ventilation Explained Clearly by MedCram.com | 2 of 5
due.label: CPAP/PEEP delivers constant pressure
due.insight: In CPAP/PEEP, you dial in a pressure rather than a volume. That pressure stays the same whether the patient is breathing in or out, maintaining airway pressure throughout the respiratory cycle.

transformed.front: A patient is on CPAP. How does the set pressure behave? A) Varies with volume B) Stays constant in and out C) Only on expiration D) Only on inspiration
transformed.back: B) Stays constant in and out
transformed.why: CPAP/PEEP dials in a pressure that stays the same whether breathing in or out, ruling out volume (A) and single-phase options (C, D).

due.label: CPAP and PEEP setting range
due.summary: CPAP and PEEP can each be set anywhere from 5 to 20 cm of water pressure.
due.userTake: Both CPAP and PEEP get dialed in somewhere in the 5 to 20 cm H2O range.

due.projectTitle: Mechanical Ventilation Explained Clearly by MedCram.com | 2 of 5
due.label: CPAP for obstructive sleep apnea
due.summary: In non-invasive mode, CPAP helps obstructive sleep apnea by keeping airway pressure high enough to hold the tongue forward and keep the airway open.
due.userTake: The constant pressure holds the tongue forward so the airway doesn't obstruct — that's why CPAP helps with sleep apnea specifically in the non-invasive setting.

due.projectTitle: Mechanical Ventilation Explained Clearly by MedCram.com | 2 of 5
due.label: PEEP keeps alveoli open (recruited)
due.insight: Positive end-expiratory pressure keeps small airways and alveolar clusters open at the end of exhalation, a process called recruitment, rather than letting them collapse to zero pressure. Higher PEEP recruits more alveoli and therefore improves oxygenation.

transformed.front:
A nurse increases a ventilated patient's PEEP. This improves oxygenation by:
A) Recruiting alveoli
B) Reducing pressure
C) Collapsing alveoli
D) Shortening exhalation
transformed.why: PEEP keeps airways and alveoli open at end-exhalation (recruitment); higher PEEP recruits more alveoli and improves O2—options B-D are not supported.

due.projectTitle: Mechanical Ventilation Explained Clearly by MedCram.com | 2 of 5
due.label: Pressure support ventilation
due.summary: Pressure support (PS) delivers a set pressure with each patient-triggered breath—unlike pressure control, you cannot set a rate. Higher pressure yields a larger breath. PS is a popular weaning mode.
due.userTake: Pressure support only fires on a patient-triggered breath and delivers a set pressure instead of a set volume — no backup rate, and it's a common weaning mode.

due.label: Pressure support is a key weaning mode
due.insight: Pressure support delivers a set pressure with each patient-triggered breath; higher pressure yields larger breaths. It is a popular mode for weaning patients off the ventilator.

transformed.front: A patient is being weaned from the ventilator. Which mode delivers a set pressure with each patient-triggered breath, where higher pressure yields larger breaths? A) Pressure support B) PEEP C) CPAP D) SIMV
transformed.why: Pressure support delivers a set pressure with each patient-triggered breath and is a popular weaning mode; the other options are not described this way in the source text.

due.projectTitle: Mechanical Ventilation Explained Clearly by MedCram.com | 2 of 5
due.label: AC (assist control)
due.body: Patient triggers the ventilator and receives a specific volume per breath; a backup rate guarantees a minimum number of breaths per minute if the patient does not breathe spontaneously.

due.projectTitle: Mechanical Ventilation Explained Clearly by MedCram.com | 2 of 5
due.label: PEEP recruits alveoli for oxygenation
due.summary: PEEP is the pressure left in the circuit at the end of exhalation, present to recruit alveoli. Higher PEEP recruits more alveoli and improves oxygenation.
due.userTake: Higher PEEP recruits more alveoli, and more recruited alveoli means better oxygenation.

due.projectTitle: Mechanical Ventilation Explained Clearly by MedCram.com | 2 of 5
due.label: Pressure control
due.body: Either the patient or the ventilator can trigger a breath; a specific pressure is delivered and then returns to baseline. Unlike pressure support, a rate can be set.

due.projectTitle: Mechanical Ventilation Explained Clearly by MedCram.com | 2 of 5
due.label: CPAP
due.body: Continuous pressure is maintained regardless of whether the patient is breathing in or out. When delivered non-invasively via mask it is called CPAP; via invasive ventilator it is called PEEP.

due.projectTitle: Mechanical Ventilation Explained Clearly by MedCram.com | 2 of 5
due.label: Pressure support
due.body: Each patient-triggered breath receives a specific amount of pressure support (typically 5–15). No rate can be set. Higher pressure yields larger breaths. Popular weaning mode.
